title: A first Python workshop, ending in a chart

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Imagine learning Python by watching a request turn into a table, and then the table turn into a chart. Each new idea has somewhere to go.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds a lot friendlier than starting with a pile of syntax.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the thinking behind Workshop1, a notebook-based Python workshop from AlgoÉTS. It's a beginner workshop, aimed at first contact with Python for finance students.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does the path look like?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It starts with setup, then moves through Python basics, calls to an API, cleaning and exploring data with pandas, and visualisation. The whole thing is nine Jupyter notebooks spread across six numbered folders.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Do I need to install anything to begin?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. The README links the first notebook straight into Google Colab, so you can open it in a browser. Or you can clone the repository and run Jupyter locally, and the setup notebooks walk through the environment.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With a final project. A notebook takes Apple's closing prices and plots them with exponential moving averages of twelve, twenty-six, fifty, a hundred and two hundred days.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's a smoothed line that follows the price, weighting recent days more. A longer one reacts more slowly, so the five curves on one chart show you fast and slow trends together.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the finale pulls the whole workshop together.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. A request, tabular data, indicator columns and a labelled chart, all in one exercise. And the page suggests classroom checks, like keeping dates in order, handling missing values on purpose and asking why a longer average responds more slowly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The next step is a batch experiment such as BatchBacktesting, another project in these notes. So it's a first step from zero to a real chart. The written page has the stage-by-stage table of notebooks.
